From: L.J. Hale, EDGWARE, Middx.

Dear Brian,

I am sorry to take up your time
on a matter not connected with
OUTLET but as you and your
brother seem to be at the nerve
centre of information concerning
the Spectrum and SAM, I hope you
will not mind.

Until I bought a SAM last year I
used a Spectrum 128, the
Sinclair original, and when I
had transferred all the programs
I wished via the Messenger,
rather than let the Spectrum
retire, I passed it on to two
young teenager friends of ours
who have done well with it.

But, disaster, one of their
schoolfriends offered them an
old ZX81 thermal printer, which
is probably faulty, and they
connected it up to the 128 and
blew it - there is no screen
output at all. I felt prety mad,
it's like losing and old friend.

There is a very good engineer at
Harrow who has carried out any
minor repairs necessary for our
family of computers in the past
but, unfortunately, he has given
up on home computers as all his
time is now taken up on commerc-
ial repairs.

Can you recommend a competent
and reliable firm or individual
who you know to undertake


Spectrum repairs, subject, of
course, these days to any spares
required being available.

I shall be most grateful for any
help you can give, as I am sure
will be the boys.

My best wished to you both for
continued success in your
enterprise.

        Yours sincerely,

        Lawrence J. Hale

From: Vincent L. Jacks, LONDON

(1) I've had my Spectrum +2 for
many a year now and the keyboard
is starting to play up on me.
Can I purchase from anywhere a
keyboard membrane for the +2
Grey? How easy is it to fit
oneself?  (I have never looked
inside my Spectrum).

(2) Does any  company  that  you
know of sell a  File  Compressor
program in order to save  memory
and disc space?

(3) I use the Uni-Dos system on
my PLUS D and using the FORMAT
option works well. It formats
the disc and does a verification
and I get no errors.

However,when I get software on
disc from anywhere else I always
get Sector Errors. Is there such
an item as a Disc Aligner?

(4) Do you know of a conversion
program for the 128K Advanced
OCP Art Studio? INDUG only do
one for the 48K version.

(5) I've noticed in the computer
magazines recently that Silica
Systems are selling the Seikosha
Sp-1900 Plus Dot Matrix printer
for `99. They say that it has
Epson and IBM emulation and a
parallel interface. Would this
printer be compatible with the
Spectrum +2 fitted with the PLUS
D Interface and if so would I
need another printer lead and
would the setup work?

(6) I have a program called T2T3
which transfers the Tasword 2
CODE files to Tasword +2
OPENTYPE files. Is there a
program available to reverse
this process?

(7) While on the subject of
Tasword,(yet again),is there a
way of getting rid of the
Spectrum Character set in the 32
column mode and if so what
address would be needed to load
a new character set? I use the
new Mini1 & Mini2 character sets
in the 64 column mode both on
the Tasword 2 and the Tasword
+2.

Could you provide me with the
address of both programs if the
above is possible?

(8) I have been trying to design
a 'readme' file which will read
the opentype files created by
Tasword +2. So far the READHELP1
is O.K. for reading the file,
however, what I can't get round
is that when the file comes to
an end I get the END OF FILE,
70:1. This when it happens -
which is every time - causes the
program to halt and I have to
then type CLOSE #*4 and then
re-run the program.

What I would like to do is STOP
the program from halting and
return to something like a menu
or some other line in the
program. How do I stop the END
OF FILE message and the program
from coming to a complete halt?

I have tried putting the TILDE
sign at the end of the file but
don't know where in the program
to adjust the line accordingly.
Can you help, please?

(9) I'm attempting to put a new
program together and am having
some difficulty with just one
part of the program. The problem
that I am having is to find out
how to stop the first page of
the CAT D1. If I attempt to use
the SPACE BAR or N to stop at
that page the program stops with
a BREAK message. If I let the
CAT D1 go on then I can't see
what files are at the upper
half. I have enclosed on disc
some DUMMY FILES so that you can
get a better idea of the
problem.

(10)I wonder if you could please
help me out with a problem that
keeps occuring while using
Tasword +2 on the Uni-Dos system
and the command (POINT #).

I usually use the README program
to read the text files created
in Tasword +2 with the margins
set at 0 and 32.

The program README came on disc
along with the main DOS system
and so I have not changed any
major lines in the program. I
note that the point command is
set thus: (POINT #4,259). While
this works with some files and
displays the text file from LINE
1, other text files start at the
middle of the text.

If I attempt to change the
command to (POINT #4,1) I just
get a lot of gibberish above the
first line of the text file.This
is most confusing as I always
start my text file at LINE 1 and
therfore cannot understand why
some start from the start and
others start around the middle.

Any help that you could offer
would be most appreciated. Many
thanks in advance of your help.

        Yours Sincerely,

           V.L. Jacks

Brian Cavers to Vincent L. Jacks

1. I do not know of any supplier
of keyboard membranes for the
Spectrum +2.You may have to bite
the bullet and send your entire
Spectrum away for repair. WTS
ELECTRONICS LTD, Studio Master
House, Chaul End Lane, Luton,
Beds, LU4 8EZ (Tel: 0582 491949)
advertise +2 repairs for `29.Yes
it is a lot to pay and you will
also be without your Spectrum
(add `5 for 24 hour courier
return service) but have you any
choice?

2. PICPACKER (OUTLET 35) is an
excellent screen compressor.
BASIC files may be compressed by
OMNIVAC (OUTLET 28).

LERM, 11 Beaconsfield Close,
Whitley Bay, NE25 9UW provide a
code compressor for `4.50. It is
not very user-friendly and only
works with tape files but it
does the job. A full review is
in OUTLET 32.

3. I don't know of such a thing
as a "disc aligner". I can only
suggest you try reducing the
step rate.I occasionally get the
same problem; it seems not all
drives are calibrated the same.
Yesterday I received a disc
formatted by Masterdos on the
SAM Coupe. It gave sector errors
when I tried to do a DIR (same
as CAT) using SAMDOS and it did
the same in my +D. However, when
I booted in Masterdos the disc
was O.K.!

Since you say you always get an
error with discs from others I
might be tempted in your shoes
to open up the drive and see if
there is any way to adjust it.

However,I do not know if this is
possible. I would have thought
that if the head starts at a
slightly different start point
along the worm screw than an
average drive then the head
would not align with the tracks
of a disc formatted on an
average drive. Does anyone know
any more about this? Surely
there must be some little screw
one can adjust or something?

Sorry, as you can see, hardware
is not my strong point!

4.My understanding is that there
is no 128K Art Studio tape to +D
conversion program available.

5. Yes, the +D printer port will
drive any normal printer with a
Centronics/Parallel socket and
which is Epson-compatible. You
need a BBC-type lead if you do
not already have one. P.B.T.
Electronics Ltd., Unit 17, Port
Talbot Workshops, Addison Road,
Port Talbot, West Glamorgan,
SA12 6HZ sell these for `7.99 +
`1 delivery.

6. Yes, our own T3TO2(OUTLET 48)
does the reverse of T2T3 and I
use it myself to convert Tasword
3 (and other) files from readers
into Tasword 2 format.

7. Some time ago I searched the
Tasword 2 to try to find where
it was pointing at the character
set in the ROM but failed. If
anyone else can find this so it
can be re-directed at another
character set then the two of us
would be very grateful!

8. There are a couple of methods
of detecting the end of the file
when reading OPENTYPE files. If
the files are of your own making
you could put some rarely-used
character such as the tilde or
a "@" character in the very last
PRINT statement. You must test
for this when inputting the text
e.g...
   10  INPUT #5; A$
   20  IF A$="@" THEN GOTO 5000

Another way which works on any
file is shown in this example...

10 OPEN #5;"NAME" IN

20 LET A$=""
30 POKE 23728,255  (stop errors)
40 INPUT #5;A$
50 POKE 23728,0 (restore errors)
60 IF A$="" THEN GOTO 90
70 PRINT A$
80 GOTO 20

90 CLOSE #*5: STOP (or whatever)

POKE 23728,255 makes the +D or
Disciple ignore errors and POKE
23278,0 restores it to normal.
You still need a test so line 20
empties the input string each
time and this is checked at line
60.

9. The same POKE 23278,255 will
solve your CAT 1 "scroll?" prob-
lem. Try...

10 POKE 23728,255  (stop errors)
20 CAT 1
30 POKE 23728,0
40 INPUT PROG
50 LOAD P PROG

If the catalogue at line 20 is
too long for one screen and the
"scroll?" message appears, it
does not matter if SPACE or N is
used to cancel the scroll as the
program will continue to the
input without losing the screen.

10. It looks as if Tas+2 may be
storing file info like margin
settings etc., at the start of
its files so...

I don't have Tasword +2 or Uni-
Dos but I would suggest trying
the following on a Tas +2 file..

10 OPEN #5;"NAME" IN
20 POINT (#5,1)
20 INPUT #5; A$   (discard this)

30 INPUT #5; A$
40 PRINT A$
50 GOTO 30

I didn't keep a copy of the Uni-
Dos file on your disc as I could
not test it so I do not know if
the above is quite the right way
to use POINT etc but the general
idea is somehow to discard the
first input (whether empty of
data or not). Perhaps someone
with Uni-Dos might comment?
                        - Brian

From: E.A. Hughes, HEREFORDSHIRE

Dear Brian and Ron,

The letter from John Hunter in
Outletters, Issue No 55 has
prompted me to write this, my
first letter to you.

Some 8 or 9 years ago when I
bought my first SPECTRUM I prod-
uced my first Calendar program
of which I was immensely proud
and, becoming bigheaded, I
decided to write a program to
give the date of Easter Sunday
whenever the appropriate month
was requested. Many frustrating
hours later my head was back to
normal size and I sought the
help of a colleague who was also
a mathematician.

Quite a while later and after
much prodding he gave me the
formula which forms the basis of
METHOD 1.

Some 18 months later I was
chatting with an acquaintance in
my local when the subject of
computers came up and I recount-
ed the story mentioned earlier.
He then told me that he, too,
had a SPECTRUM and a program to
calculate the date of Easter
Sunday that he had copied from a
magazine and would I like to
swap programs. His program forms
the basis of METHOD 2.

Then through the letter box pops
OUTLET No. 55 containing the
letter and another formula from
John Hunter - METHOD 3.

However,when you run the program
"EASTER" [in ADDENDERS] you will
see that the three methods do
not always agree as to the
correct date of Easter Sunday.

If you go to your Local Library
and check the dates against
those given in Whittakers
Almanac, you will see that only
those dates given by Method 1
are consistently correct.

I must confess that I cannot
explain the reason for this but
I am sure that among your
readers there is someone who
can, and I am also sure that
some of them will also have some
other formula to calculate the
date of Easter.

Perhaps they could send it/them
to OUTLET for our edification.

By the way I do not seem to have
the "KWICAL" program mentioned
by John Hunter. In which issue
of OUTLET did it appear?

        Yours E.A.Hughes

P.S. Many thanks for persuading
me to treat myself to a +D for
Christmas. How did I tolerate
tape for so long?

Brian Cavers to Mr. E. A. Hughes


Many thanks. Calculating Easter
day is becoming quite a popular
interest.

The KWICAL program was in the
SAM version of OUTLET 41 only.

                          Brian

From Brian Cavers to Bob Randall

The program to compress BASIC is
OMNIVAC in OUTLET 28.It replaces
0 with NOT PI, 1 with  SGN PI,
puts values below 256 into CODE
statements and above into VAL's.

DEVAL 2 in OUTLET 56 will partly
restore such compressed programs
by removing the VALs but not the
NOT PI's, SGN PI's or CODEs.

You say it is "not possible" to
"find out how a program works"
but there is no problem recog-
nizing the value in say VAL"123"
and also NOT PI and SGN PI once
you know they represent 0 and 1.
Only CODE might be awkward but
this is what you do...

In 48K BASIC you can simply type
print CODE "BRIGHT" to reveal
its value. For command words you
first type THEN thus... PRINT
CODE "THEN PLOT" then delete the
"THEN" part.

In 128K BASIC you need to enter
INPUT A$:PRINT A$ (can be a
direct command) and then repeat
as for 48K BASIC.

If you've the original Spectrum
manual, all these values are
listed for easy reference but
you can easily print such a list
with FOR N=32 TO 255:LPRINT N;"
";CHR$ N: NEXT N (this must be
in "expanded" mode -as you would
use for LLIST.
                      - Brian

From: A. de B. Adam, WOKING

Thank you for continuing with
"OUTLET". Please can you help me
to get more satisfaction from
your programs in the following
ways.

Can you let me know how to ex-
tract the individual programs so
I can file them under particular
headings for quicker extraction
and use. I have a +D Interface
and drive from Datel but do not
know how to use it properly.
With your permission, can you
please allow me to extract pro-
grams on fractals and introduce
colour and variations to them
and explain to me how to extract
them?
                       -Arthur

Brian Cavers to Arthur de B Adam

Yes, press BREAK (ESC on the SAM
Coupe) and enter BASIC (select
128K or +3 BASIC if a 128K
machine). To re-save the program
put a disc in the drive or start
the tape and enter...

 RUN 9972   (+3)

 RUN 9982   (+D,M/Drive,Opus)

 RUN 9983   (tape)

 RS         (SAM Coupe)

Occasionally some programs are
invisible or garbled when listed
in 128K so don't LOAD them but
merge them with MERGE..."name"

When reloading, if the message,
"file not found" appears (or if
a tape version is waiting to
load another file) then press
BREAK (ESC on SAM) and note down
the line number shown at the
bottom of the screen. e.g., 9010
in this example...

   L BREAK into program 9010:1


Enter LIST 9010 to see what file
needs to be copied. Use the COPY
command on +3 and SAM or SAVE TO
on +D and Disciple(see manuals).
These may also be used with the
main BASIC program if preferred.
If anyone needs any help with a
particular program,please write
to me.

Yes, you can certainly extract
programs on fractals or any
others you like. Feel free to
BREAK into OUTLET programs and
modify them as much as you like
for your own use. Remember, you
must not give away or sell any
OUTLET programs unless they are
marked "FREEWARE" or public
domain but you can extract them,
alter them, adjust them and re-
save them for your own use.

Some programs are machine code
and cannot be modified or listed
by beginners. Experience is
needed to modify even BASIC and
if you don't even know how to
BREAK into and extract programs
then you may not be able to
rewrite them to any great extent
-but experiment and learn!-Brian

From: J.P. Messenbird, SURREY

Dear Ron and Brian,

Will OUTLET stay faithful to
Spectrum computer owners or will
it eventually become an all-SAM
Coupe Magazine? The reason I am
asking is because the decline of
the amount of Spectrum software
in the shops recently. In some
places you can only buy budget
(i.e. `3.99) software for the
Spectrum. All their full price
software tends to be for the
Amiga or Atari ST computers.

YOUR SINCLAIR magazine has
started a 'Support Our Speccy'
campaign, because, naturally
they are concerned about this.

I hope you will stick with us
Spectrum owners. It will be a
very sad day if OUTLET became
an all-SAM Coupe magazine.

        Best wishes from,

         J.P. Messenbird

Brian Cavers to J.P. Messenbird

The fate of OUTLET is not linked
to the decline of games software
but to support by its readers.It
is named "OUTLET" because it is
intended to be YOUR outlet for
YOUR ideas and programs.

It's always been a priority with
us to provide a service and not
simply to profit. Still,we can't
live on thin air and must make
enough to keep going! If anyone
wants to support OUTLET then
suggestions how to increase our
readership would be welcomed!

The SAM is not favoured over the
Spectrum by either Ron or myself
so you need have no fears about
that.                   - Brian.

10 OPEN #5;"NAME" IN

20 LET A$="" 30 POKE 23728,255  (stop errors) 40 INPUT #5;A$ 50 POKE 23728,0 (restore errors) 60 IF A$="" THEN GOTO 90 70 PRINT A$ 80 GOTO 20

10 OPEN #5;"NAME" IN 20 POINT (#5,1) 20 INPUT #5; A$   (discard this)

The program to compress BASIC is OMNIVAC in OUTLET 28.It replaces 0 with NOT PI, 1 with  SGN PI, puts values below 256 into CODE statements and above into VAL's.

DEVAL 2 in OUTLET 56 will partly restore such compressed programs by removing the VALs but not the NOT PI's, SGN PI's or CODEs.

You say it is "not possible" to "find out how a program works" but there is no problem recog- nizing the value in say VAL"123" and also NOT PI and SGN PI once you know they represent 0 and 1. Only CODE might be awkward but this is what you do...

In 48K BASIC you can simply type print CODE "BRIGHT" to reveal its value. For command words you first type THEN thus... PRINT CODE "THEN PLOT" then delete the "THEN" part.

In 128K BASIC you need to enter INPUT A$:PRINT A$ (can be a direct command) and then repeat as for 48K BASIC.

Программа для сжатия BASIC — это OMNIVAC в OUTLET 28. Она заменяет 0 на NOT PI, 1 на SGN PI, помещает значения до 256 в операторы CODE, а значения выше — в VAL.

В 48K BASIC вы можете просто ввести print CODE "BRIGHT", чтобы узнать его значение. Для командных слов сначала введите THEN, таким образом: PRINT CODE "THEN PLOT", а затем удалите часть "THEN".

В 128K BASIC вам нужно ввести INPUT A$:PRINT A$ (может быть прямой командой), а затем повторить как для 48K BASIC.

Если у вас есть оригинальное руководство к Spectrum, все эти значения перечислены для удобства, но вы можете легко распечатать такой список с помощью FOR N=32 TO 255:LPRINT N;" ";CHR$ N: NEXT N (это должно быть в «расширенном» режиме, как для LLIST).

```

Иногда некоторые программы невидимы или искажены при листинге в 128K, поэтому не загружайте (LOAD) их, а объединяйте с помощью MERGE "name".

 L BREAK into program 9010:1
```
